claim: Hereditary diffuse leukoencephalopathy with axonal spheroids (HDLS) is a rare, fatal, adult-onset neurodegenerative disease that is most often caused by mutations affecting the colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R).
source: Hereditary diffuse leukoencephalopathy with axonal spheroids (HDLS) is a rare, fatal, adult-onset neurodegenerative disease that is most often caused by mutations affecting the colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background information about HDLS.

claim: Macrophages derived from iPSC (iMacs) of HDLS patients exhibited a metabolic shift toward the glycolytic pathway.
source: Macrophages derived from iPSC (iMacs) of patients exhibited a metabolic shift toward the glycolytic pathway and reduced CSF-1 sensitivity, which was associated with higher levels of IL-1β production and an activated inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This finding is reported in the abstract as a result from the study's experiments.

claim: HDLS patient-derived iMacs showed reduced CSF-1 sensitivity.
source: Macrophages derived from iPSC (iMacs) of patients exhibited a metabolic shift toward the glycolytic pathway and reduced CSF-1 sensitivity, which was associated with higher levels of IL-1β production and an activated inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an experimental finding.

claim: HDLS patient-derived iMacs showed higher levels of IL-1β production.
source: Macrophages derived from iPSC (iMacs) of patients exhibited a metabolic shift toward the glycolytic pathway and reduced CSF-1 sensitivity, which was associated with higher levels of IL-1β production and an activated inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is reported in the abstract as a key experimental finding.

claim: HDLS patient-derived iMacs exhibited an activated inflammatory phenotype.
source: Macrophages derived from iPSC (iMacs) of patients exhibited a metabolic shift toward the glycolytic pathway and reduced CSF-1 sensitivity, which was associated with higher levels of IL-1β production and an activated inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a characterization of the cells based on experimental data.

claim: Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that iMacs adopt a reactive state that leads to impaired regulation of neuronal cell populations in organoid cultures.
source: Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that iMacs adopt a reactive state that leads to impaired regulation of neuronal cell populations in organoid cultures, thereby identifying microglial dysregulation and specifically IL-1β production as key contributors to the degenerative neuro-environment in HDLS.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from bulk RNA sequencing experiments.

claim: Microglial dysregulation is a key contributor to the degenerative neuro-environment in HDLS.
source: Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that iMacs adopt a reactive state that leads to impaired regulation of neuronal cell populations in organoid cultures, thereby identifying microglial dysregulation and specifically IL-1β production as key contributors to the degenerative neuro-environment in HDLS.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: IL-1β production is a key contributor to the degenerative neuro-environment in HDLS.
source: Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that iMacs adopt a reactive state that leads to impaired regulation of neuronal cell populations in organoid cultures, thereby identifying microglial dysregulation and specifically IL-1β production as key contributors to the degenerative neuro-environment in HDLS.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: HDLS is characterized by patchy axonal swellings (spheroids) and demyelination that result in the alteration of the white matter of the brain.
source: Hereditary diffused leukoencephalopathy with axonal spheroids (HDLS) – also known as adult-onset leukodystrophy with axonal spheroids and pigmented glia (ALSP), is a rare, inherited, autosomal dominant, neurodegenerative disease that is characterized by patchy axonal swellings (spheroids) and demyelination that result in the alteration of the white matter of the brain (Marotti et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: In 2021, it was estimated that approximately a quarter of a million people globally are affected by HDLS.
source: Although detailed epidemiological data are lacking, in 2021, it was estimated that approximately a quarter of a million people globally are affected by the condition (Papapetropoulos et al., 2021)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to a 2021 publication.

claim: HDLS is caused by mutations affecting the colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R).
source: For more than a decade, we have known that HDLS is caused by mutations affecting the colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R) (Rademakers et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: HDLS mutations most often occur in the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) of CSF-1R.
source: For more than a decade, we have known that HDLS is caused by mutations affecting the colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R) (Rademakers et al., 2011) which most often occur in the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (Zhuang et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: HDLS mutations lead to reduced auto-phosphorylation in response to CSF-1, which results in impaired downstream signaling.
source: which most often occur in the tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) (Zhuang et al., 2020), and lead to reduced auto-phosphorylation in response to CSF-1, which results in impaired downstream signaling (Zhuang et al., 2020; Pridans et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior studies.

claim: HDLS mutations most profoundly affect microglia.
source: These mutations most profoundly affect microglia (Biundo et al., 2021), the specialized brain-resident macrophages that play critical roles in brain development and homeostasis (Tay et al., 2017; Hammond et al., 2018) as well as in a wide range of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases (Bachiller et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: Microglia play critical roles in brain development and homeostasis.
source: These mutations most profoundly affect microglia (Biundo et al., 2021), the specialized brain-resident macrophages that play critical roles in brain development and homeostasis (Tay et al., 2017; Hammond et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior work.

claim: Microglia play roles in a wide range of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: the specialized brain-resident macrophages that play critical roles in brain development and homeostasis (Tay et al., 2017; Hammond et al., 2018) as well as in a wide range of neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases (Bachiller et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: Patients with HDLS have few, small, microglia that are distributed abnormally within the neocortex.
source: Patients with HDLS have few, small, microglia that are distributed abnormally within the neocortex and that express low levels of the homeostatic marker P2RY12 and high levels of the inflammatory marker CD68, compared to healthy controls (Kempthorne et al., 2020; Konno et al., 2018; Tada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior studies.

claim: HDLS patient microglia express low levels of the homeostatic marker P2RY12.
source: Patients with HDLS have few, small, microglia that are distributed abnormally within the neocortex and that express low levels of the homeostatic marker P2RY12 and high levels of the inflammatory marker CD68, compared to healthy controls (Kempthorne et al., 2020; Konno et al., 2018; Tada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior literature.

claim: HDLS patient microglia express high levels of the inflammatory marker CD68.
source: Patients with HDLS have few, small, microglia that are distributed abnormally within the neocortex and that express low levels of the homeostatic marker P2RY12 and high levels of the inflammatory marker CD68, compared to healthy controls (Kempthorne et al., 2020; Konno et al., 2018; Tada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior studies.

claim: The earliest haplo-insufficient Csf-1r+/− mice model exhibited microgliosis within brain regions.
source: the earliest haplo-insufficient Csf-1r+/− mice model exhibited microgliosis within brain regions (Chitu et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: Microgliosis was not recapitulated in a Csf-1r knockout rat model.
source: the earliest haplo-insufficient Csf-1r+/− mice model exhibited microgliosis within brain regions (Chitu et al., 2015), but this was not recapitulated in a later Csf-1r knockout rat model (Patkar et al., 2021)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: An orthologous mouse model has phenocopied the reduced microglia density seen in patients with HDLS but does not exhibit brain pathology.
source: while a subsequent orthologous mouse model has phenocopied the reduced microglia density seen in patients with HDLS but does not exhibit brain pathology (Stables et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: A zebrafish model of HDLS saw reduced microglia during brain development.
source: A zebrafish model of HDLS similarly saw reduced microglia during brain development (Berdowski et al., 2022)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior literature.

claim: The zebrafish model does not offer the opportunity to study pathology associated with adult-onset neurodegenerative diseases.
source: A zebrafish model of HDLS similarly saw reduced microglia during brain development (Berdowski et al., 2022), but does not offer the opportunity to study pathology associated with adult-onset neurodegenerative diseases (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: Dermal fibroblasts were isolated from skin biopsies taken from two patients with HDLS with confirmed mutations in the TDK region of the CSF-1R gene.
source: We first isolated dermal fibroblasts from skin biopsies taken from two patients with HDLS and confirmed mutations in the TDK region of the CSF-1R gene (HD1, HD2; clinical characteristics shown in Supplementary file 1, table S1)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental procedures.

claim: iPSC-like colonies emerged 4 to 5 weeks post-transfection.
source: Four to five weeks post-transfection, we observed iPSC-like colonies emerging (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing experimental observations.

claim: Successful reprogramming was confirmed by visualization of pluripotency markers including SOX2, OCT4, TRA-1-60, and SSEA-4.
source: We confirmed successful reprogramming by visualization of pluripotency markers including SOX2 and OCT4 (nuclear markers), and TRA-1-60 and SSEA-4 (intracellular marker), by immunofluorescence (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The iPSC clones had normal karyotype.
source: We also confirmed that these clones had normal karyotype (Figure 1E)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Isogenic controls were generated from Mut HD1 and Mut HD2 iPSC cell lines.
source: We then generated isogenic from Mut HD1 and Mut HD2 iPSC cell lines which we termed IsoHD1 and IsoHD2, respectively, as controls (see Methods).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental approach.

claim: No off-target events were identified in the isogenic controls.
source: Clones that were karyotypically normal were used for downstream experiments alongside their mutant counterparts (Figure 1B), with no off-target events identified (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: iMacs were generated from HDLS donor-derived iPSC using a serum-free protocol that recapitulates the generation of in vivo microglial progenitor cells.
source: We next sought to differentiate primitive microglia-like macrophages from patient-derived iPSC cell lines (iMacs) using our serum-free protocol that faithfully recapitulates the generation of in vivo microglial progenitor cells (Takata et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to the protocol.

claim: The yield of iMacs from iPSC varied between cultures.
source: Although HDLS mutation downregulates the sensitivity of CSF-1R to its ligand (Pridans et al., 2013), we were able to successfully generate iMacs using this protocol: the yield of iMacs from iPSC varied between cultures (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Flow cytometry confirmed consistent macrophage-like phenotype of iMacs with abundant expression of CD45 and CD14.
source: flow cytometry confirmed their consistent macrophage-like phenotype, with abundant expression of CD45 and CD14 (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Giemsa staining showed that iMacs exhibited comparable morphology between donors.
source: Giemsa staining showed that iMacs exhibited comparable morphology between donors (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: All iMac cultures were equally able to take up PE-labeled beads.
source: Functionally, all iMac cultures were equally able to take up PE-labeled beads that were detectable within their cell bodies (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The level of actin-dependent phagocytosis of pHrodo beads was comparable among CD45-expressing cells from all cultures.
source: flow cytometry confirmed that the level of actin-dependent phagocytosis of pHrodo beads was comparable among CD45-expressing cells from all cultures (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Even with high concentrations of CSF-1, relatively few mutant cells survived across 7 days of culture.
source: As expected, even with high concentrations of CSF-1, relatively few mutant cells survived across 7 days of culture; by contrast, even low CSF-1 levels allowed significantly more isogenic cells to survive (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Even low CSF-1 levels allowed significantly more isogenic cells to survive compared to mutant cells.
source: As expected, even with high concentrations of CSF-1, relatively few mutant cells survived across 7 days of culture; by contrast, even low CSF-1 levels allowed significantly more isogenic cells to survive (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Patterns of gene expression differed markedly between mutant and isogenic iMacs.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) showed that patterns of gene expression differed markedly between mutant and isogenic iMacs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing RNA-seq analysis.

claim: HD1 Mut iMacs had higher expression of genes involved in pathways related to proliferation.
source: Among cell cultures from HD1, mutant iMacs exhibited patterns of gene expression consistent with a more reactive state compared to isogenic CSF-1R-restored HD1: HD1 Mut had higher expression of genes involved in pathways related to proliferation (IGF2, MYBL2, STAT1, INCEP, TGFA)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing transcriptomic analysis.

claim: HD1 Mut iMacs had higher expression of genes involved in the defense response to virus.
source: HD1 Mut had higher expression of genes involved in pathways related to proliferation (IGF2, MYBL2, STAT1, INCEP, TGFA) and the defense response to virus (IFI27, IFI44L, STAT1, MX1, IFIT3)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Iso HD1 iMacs expressed high levels of genes involved in chemokine-related responses and signaling pathways.
source: while Iso HD1 iMacs expressed high levels of genes involved in chemokine-related responses and signaling pathways (CXCL2, ADAM8, CCL31L, CCL5), as well as leukocyte migration and chemotaxis (CXCL3, CCL13, CCL2, E5AR1, C3AR1) (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Iso HD1 iMacs expressed high levels of genes involved in leukocyte migration and chemotaxis.
source: while Iso HD1 iMacs expressed high levels of genes involved in chemokine-related responses and signaling pathways (CXCL2, ADAM8, CCL31L, CCL5), as well as leukocyte migration and chemotaxis (CXCL3, CCL13, CCL2, E5AR1, C3AR1) (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: HD2 Mut iMacs showed upregulated gene expression for the defensive response to virus.
source: We observed a similar transcriptomic profile in HD2-derived iMacs: HD2 Mut showed upregulated gene expression for the defensive response to virus, while isogenic HD2 iMacs exhibited high expression levels of genes involved in leukocyte migration and chemotaxis (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Isogenic HD2 iMacs exhibited high expression levels of genes involved in leukocyte migration and chemotaxis.
source: We observed a similar transcriptomic profile in HD2-derived iMacs: HD2 Mut showed upregulated gene expression for the defensive response to virus, while isogenic HD2 iMacs exhibited high expression levels of genes involved in leukocyte migration and chemotaxis (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: An upregulation of the immature myeloid cell marker MPO was observed within mutant iMac of both cell lines.
source: Additionally, an upregulation of the immature myeloid cell marker MPO (Pinkus and Pinkus, 1991), and a reduced expression of mature macrophage marker MARCO (Elchaninov et al., 2021) was observed within mutant iMac of both cell lines.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior literature.

claim: A reduced expression of mature macrophage marker MARCO was observed within mutant iMac of both cell lines.
source: Additionally, an upregulation of the immature myeloid cell marker MPO (Pinkus and Pinkus, 1991), and a reduced expression of mature macrophage marker MARCO (Elchaninov et al., 2021) was observed within mutant iMac of both cell lines.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to prior literature.

claim: CSF-1R-mutant iMacs from both HD1 and HD2 had a significant overall increase in glycolytic function.
source: this showed that CSF-1R-mutant iMacs from both HD1 and HD2 had a significant overall increase in glycolytic function (Figure 3G, O).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3G, O.

claim: CSF-1R mutation was associated with significantly increased glycolytic capacity and glycolytic reserve in both HD1 and HD2 iMacs.
source: Although the magnitude of the difference between iMac HD1 and HD2 and their respective CSF-1R-restored counterparts varied, in both cases, CSF-1R mutation was associated with significantly increased glycolytic capacity and glycolytic reserve.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing metabolic profiling.

claim: Both sets of iMacs showed a trend toward higher OCR values in the presence of mutated CSF-1R.
source: As before, although the magnitude of effect was less for cells from HD1, both sets of iMacs showed a similar trend toward higher OCR values, and greater capacity for basal respiration, ATP production, and maximal respiratory capacity in the presence of mutated CSF-1R
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing metabolic analysis.

claim: HD2 Mut cells showed statistically significant differences in basal respiration, ATP production, and maximal respiratory capacity.
source: in the case of HD2 Mut cells, these differences achieved statistical significance across all three bioenergetic parameters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing metabolic analysis.

claim: The absence of fully functional CSF-1R in cells from HD1 and HD2 is associated with an upregulated glycolytic metabolic profile.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the absence of fully functional CSF-1R in cells from HD1 and HD2 is associated with an upregulated glycolytic metabolic profile, which is cells from HD2 is clearly accompanied by a higher mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation rate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of metabolic findings.

claim: In cells from HD2, the upregulated glycolytic profile is accompanied by a higher mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation rate.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the absence of fully functional CSF-1R in cells from HD1 and HD2 is associated with an upregulated glycolytic metabolic profile, which is cells from HD2 is clearly accompanied by a higher mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation rate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of metabolic findings.

claim: Macrophages from patients with HDLS have an altered metabolic profile that correlates with their higher activation status.
source: This suggests that macrophages from patients with HDLS have an altered metabolic profile that correlates with their higher activation status and could contribute to disease pathology.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Both iMac lines from both patients effectively phagocytosed apoptotic but not control, non-UV-irradiated, SH-SY5Y cells, in an actin-dependent manner.
source: Both iMac lines (CSF-1R mutant and isogenic) from both patients effectively phagocytosed apoptotic but not control, non-UV-irradiated, SH-SY5Y cells, in an actin-dependent manner (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A significant and specific increase in IL-1β transcription was observed in CSF-1R mutated iMacs from both HD1 and HD2 when exposed to apoptotic cells, compared with their isogenic counterparts.
source: We observed a significant and specific increase in IL-1β transcription in CSF-1R mutated iMacs from both HD1 and HD2 when exposed to apoptotic cells, compared with their isogenic counterparts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cytokine expression analysis.

claim: Mut HD2 cells exhibited significantly increased transcription of the gene encoding TGF-β when co-cultured with UV-treated cells.
source: Among the anti-inflammatory cytokines, Mut HD2 cells exhibited significantly increased transcription of the gene encoding TGF-β when co-cultured with UV-treated cells, alongside high baseline levels of IL-12 and TGF-β in control cultures compared to isogenic HD2 iMacs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cytokine expression analysis.

claim: All CSF-1R mutant iMac groups had higher levels of transcription of most pro-inflammatory cytokines at baseline than did their CSF-1R-restored counterparts.
source: Interestingly, all CSF-1R mutant iMac groups had higher levels of transcription of most pro-inflammatory cytokines at baseline, consistent with their activated/reactive transcriptional profile, than did their CSF-1R-restored counterparts (Figure 4A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: iMacs expressing the microglial marker IBA-1 were mostly located on the surface of the organoids.
source: This showed that iMacs expressing the microglial marker IBA-1, were mostly located on the surface of the organoids (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Neural epithelial rosettes were present in all of the organoids, consisting mostly of SOX2+ NPCs.
source: In all of the organoids, neural epithelial rosettes were present, consisting mostly of SOX2+ NPCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Organoids to which iMacs were not added did not contain any IBA-1+ cells.
source: Importantly, organoids to which we did not add iMacs did not contain any IBA-1+ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: HD1 iMacs after co-culture had profoundly altered their gene expression compared to day 31 non-co-cultured iMacs.
source: Compared to day 31 non-co-cultured iMacs, HD1 iMacs after co-culture had profoundly altered their gene expression (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Upregulated DEGs in HD1 iMacs after co-culture showed an increase in pathways characteristic of microglial functions in the brain such as central nervous system and brain development.
source: with the upregulated DEGs showing an increase in various pathways that are characteristic of microglial functions in the brain such as central nervous system and brain development (CNTN1, ZIC2, EFNA2, GLI3), synapse organization, synapse and neuron organization and development (SLC1A1, DGKB, TRIM67), as well as neurogenesis (CHD11, ADCYAP1) (Figure 5F, G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F, G.

claim: Patterns of gene expression were markedly different between co-cultured and non-co-cultured HD2 iMac populations.
source: Likewise, for HD2 iMacs, PCA also suggested that their patterns of gene expression were markedly different between co-cultured and non-co-cultured populations (Figure 5H)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: GO analysis of upregulated DEGs in HD2 iMacs revealed an increase in pathways linked with typical microglial functions in the brain such as glial cell differentiation and gliogenesis.
source: while GO analysis of the upregulated DEGs revealed an increase in various pathways linked with typical microglial functions in the brain such as glial cell differentiation and gliogenesis (CLU, MDK, CXCR4, RELN, TMEM98, TUBA1A), axonal development (UCHL1, MAP1B, CRABP2, TUBB2B, LGI1) as well as forebrain development (TUBB2B, MDK, CXCR4, RELN, LHX2) (Figure 5I, J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5I, J.

claim: iMacs undergoing co-culture with forebrain organoids have differentiated to a certain extent into microglia-like cells.
source: This shows that iMacs undergoing co-culture with forebrain organoids have differentiated to a certain extent, into microglia-like cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the transcriptomic data.

claim: Co-culture of IsoHD1 organoid with IsoHD1 iMac saw a significant reduction in the neuronal population when compared to control organoids that did not undergo co-culture.
source: Co-culture of IsoHD1 organoid with IsoHD1 iMac saw a significant reduction in the neuronal population when compared to control organoids that did not underwent co-culture.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing cell population analysis.

claim: Co-culture with mutant HD1 iMac saw a smaller degree of neurons reduction but was not significant.
source: Conversely, co-culture with mutant HD1 iMac saw a smaller degree of neurons reduction but was not significant (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Transcriptomic analysis of the neurons of HD2 co-culture saw the mutant iMac co-culture having upregulated expression of genes associated with mitochondrial respiration.
source: Transcriptomic analysis of the neurons of HD2 co-culture saw the mutant iMac co-culture having upregulated expression of genes associated with mitochondrial respiration (BCS1L, MRPL18, TSFM, MRPL11, MRPS30) but this phenomenon was not present in the isogenic iMac co-culture (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Transcriptomic analysis of the NPCs of HD2 co-culture saw the isogenic iMac co-culture having upregulated expression of genes associated with mitochondrial respiration.
source: Conversely, transcriptomic analysis of the NPCs of HD2 co-culture saw the isogenic iMac co-culture having upregulated expression of genes associated with mitochondrial respiration (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: HDLS mutation affects neuronal population in a microglia-dependent manner and this phenomenon is variable and mutation dependent.
source: Taken together, our model suggests that HDLS mutation affects neuronal population in a microglia-dependent manner and that this phenomenon is variable and mutation dependent.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Rodent models do not faithfully recapitulate the disease phenotype in humans.
source: Efforts to elucidate the functional or dysfunctional aspects of the causative mutations in the CSF-1R gene have been hampered by the lack of an accurate disease model that recapitulates the human pathology: although rodent and zebrafish models have been generated and imparted valuable insights toward HDLS (Chitu et al., 2015; Patkar et al., 2021; Stables et al., 2022; Berdowski et al., 2022), discrepancies and limitations in each case have led to incomplete recapitulation of the disease's pathology, specifically in microglia numbers within brain regions and the effects on respective cognitive and sensorimotor tests.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior literature.

claim: No other in vitro studies have yet reverted the causative mutation to wild type.
source: While the generation of an HDLS donor-derived iPSC cell line has been reported (Wu et al., 2021), no other in vitro studies have yet reverted the causative mutation to wild type; a necessary step to understanding the direct impacts of diminished/absent CSF-1R signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation to prior work.

claim: iMac yield varied greatly between the cell lines with a 50% lower yield for Mut HD1 compared to IsoHD1.
source: Although we were able to generate phenotypically and functionally similar iMac across these lines for example for phagocytic capability, iMac yield varied greatly between the cell lines with a 50% lower yield for Mut HD1 compared to IsoHD1 and, conversely, a higher yield for Mut HD2 200% compared to IsoHD2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion describing experimental observations.

claim: Mut HD2 had a higher yield (200%) compared to IsoHD2.
source: Although we were able to generate phenotypically and functionally similar iMac across these lines for example for phagocytic capability, iMac yield varied greatly between the cell lines with a 50% lower yield for Mut HD1 compared to IsoHD1 and, conversely, a higher yield for Mut HD2 200% compared to IsoHD2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion describing experimental observations.

claim: The nonsense mutation identified in HD2 could more profoundly affect receptor signaling.
source: This fundamental difference could be attributed to their respective mutations: the nonsense mutation identified in HD2 could not only more profoundly affect receptor signaling, but might also be a major factor during the course of gene editing leading to incomplete reversion to wild type at the epigenetic level, which we speculate was not the case for IsoHD1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation about the findings.

claim: Higher levels of baseline pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine production in the control group without apoptotic cells were observed within HD1 mutant, and both HD1 and HD2 mutant iMacs.
source: Importantly, higher levels of baseline pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine production in the control group without apoptotic cells were observed within HD1 mutant, and both HD1 and HD2 mutant iMacs, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion describing experimental findings.

claim: Mutant iMacs are innately in a more reactive or activated state when compared to isogenic iMacs.
source: This suggests that mutant iMacs are innately in a more reactive or activated state when compared to isogenic iMacs and could reflect the reactive phenotype of HDLS-associated microglia and macrophage identified in vivo (Kempthorne et al., 2020; Tada et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation with citations to prior work.

claim: Isogenic iMacs adopt less of the reactive phenotype with the reverted mutation.
source: Conversely, isogenic iMacs seems to adopt less of the reactive phenotype with the reverted mutation as identified with an overall lesser cytokine production level.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Addition of iMac modulated NPC differentiation, limiting their proliferation and promoting axonogenesis, resulting in a reduction of co-culture organoid size.
source: Here, while we noticed a significant decreased in the size of isogenic HD1 forebrains co-cultured with isogenic HD1 iMac compared to isogenic HD1 organoids, we did not measure any significant change in organoid size in the isogenic HD1 organoids co-cultured with mutant HD1 iMacs. This suggested that the crosstalk between iMicro and NPC is dysregulated in the context of the HD1 mutation. Since we showed that such size reduction is mediated by cholesterol transfer from iMicro to NPC, further work will be required to characterize cholesterol metabolism of HD iMac.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with reference to prior work (Park et al., 2023).

claim: The crosstalk between iMicro and NPC is dysregulated in the context of the HD1 mutation.
source: This suggested that the crosstalk between iMicro and NPC is dysregulated in the context of the HD1 mutation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Mutated iMicro can change the states of non-mutated isogenic organoid cells.
source: This suggests increased metabolic rates in these respective populations that are contributed to by the different variants of iMac during co-culture, and show that mutated iMicro can change the states of non-mutated isogenic organoid cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: CSF-1R mutation in HDLS may cause subtle yet impactful disruptions to microglia homeostasis due to abnormal metabolic functions in the developing fetal brain.
source: Altogether, we propose that CSF-1R mutation in HDLS may cause subtle yet impactful disruptions to microglia homeostasis due to abnormal metabolic functions in the developing fetal brain, that subsequently compound and result in aberrant microglia functions during adulthood.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposed model.

claim: Disruptions to microglia homeostasis could be mediated by upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokine production such as IL-1β at a basal level or upon clearing of cellular debris during development and adulthood homeostasis.
source: This could also be mediated by upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokine production such as IL-1β at a basal level or upon clearing of cellular debris during development and adulthood homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposed mechanism.

claim: Postmortem brain sample analysis revealed elevated levels of IL-1β production, including around amyloid beta plaques in Alzheimer's disease.
source: IL-1β is of particular interest as numerous studies reported the role of IL-1β in neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration especially within the field of Alzheimer's disease: for example, postmortem brain sample analysis revealed elevated levels of Il-1β production, including around amyloid beta plaques; all suggestive of pathology-associated inflammation (Cacabelos et al., 1994; Shaftel et al., 2008; Italiani et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to prior literature.

claim: CSF-1R+/− mutant microglia have a predisposition toward increased secretion of IL-1β.
source: Hence, we speculate that in CSF-1R+/− mutant microglia, which already have a predisposition toward increased secretion of IL-1β, are constantly being activated by IL-1β, either autocrine or paracrine, creating a dysfunctional neuro-environment that contributes to HDLS pathology.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as speculation based on the findings.

claim: Canakinumab targeting IL-1β could be a potential target for therapy and may help to ameliorate HDLS pathology.
source: As such, experimental models looking to block or reduce IL-1β levels in the brain using the human mAb, canakinumab, targeting the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-1β (Ridker et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2022), during both health and disease could be a potential target for therapy and may help to ameliorate HDLS pathology.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposed therapeutic approach with citations.
